pp:ce:2015:q1.question:
For what value of p the following set of equations will have no solution?
2x+3y=5
3x+py=10

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Linear Algebra
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given system of equations has no solution if the lines are parallel i.e., their slopes are equal

$$\begin{aligned}     \frac{2}{3}&=\frac{3}{p} \\ \Rightarrow   \;\;   p&=4.5 \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q2.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 2
pp:ce:2015:q2.question: The integral $\int_{x_1}^{x_2}x^{2}dx$ with ${x_1} \gt {x_2} \gt 0$ is evaluated analytically as well as numerically using a single application of the trapezoidal rule. If I is the exact value of the integral obtained analytically and J is the approximate  value  obtained  using  the trapezoidal rule, which of the following statements is correct about their relationship?
options: Insufficient data to determine the relationship

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Numerical Methods
detailed_solution.markdown: Exact value is computed by integration which follows the exact shape of graph while computing the area. Whereas, in Trapezoidal rule, the lines joining each points are considered straight lines which is not the exact variation of graph all the time like as shown figure. $\therefore J\gt I$ OR $\text{Error } =-\frac{h^{3}}{12}{f}''\left ( \Im \right )\times n_{i}$ Here, $f\left ( x \right )=x^{2}$ or, ${f}'\left ( x \right )=2x$ or, ${f}''\left ( x \right )=2\gt 0$ Since ${f}''\left ( x \right )$ is positive, the error is negative. Since error = exact-approximate. $=I-J$ and since error is negative in this case $J\gt I$ is true.

pp:ce:2015:q3.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 3
pp:ce:2015:q3.question:
Consider the following probability mass function (p.m.f) of a random variable X :
$$p(x,q)=\begin{cases} q & \text{ if } X=0\\ 1-q& \text{ if } X=1 \\ 0 & \text otherwise \end{cases}$$
If q = 0.4, the variance of X is _______.

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Probability and Statistics
detailed_solution.markdown: Given, $\; \; \; \; q=0.4$ Required value $=V\left ( X \right )=E\left ( X^{2} \right )-\left [ E\left ( X \right ) \right ]^{2}$ $E\left ( X \right )=\sum_{i}^{}\, X_{i}p_{i}=0\times 0.4+1\times 0.6=0.6$ $E\left ( X^{2} \right )=\sum_{i}^{}\, X_{i}^{2}p_{i}=0^{2}\times 0.4+1^{2}\times 0.6=0.6$ $\therefore \; \; \; V\left ( X \right )=E\left ( X^{2} \right )-\left [ E\left ( X \right ) \right ]^{2}=0.6-0.36=0.24$

pp:ce:2015:q4.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 4
pp:ce:2015:q4.question:
Workability of concrete can be measured using slump, compaction factor and Vebe time. Consider the following statements for workability of concrete:

(i) As the slump increases, the Vebe time increases
(ii) As the slump increases, the compaction factor increases

Which of the following is TRUE?

primary.subtopicLabel: Working Stress and Limit State Method

detailed_solution.concept: RCC Structures - Working Stress and Limit State Method
detailed_solution.markdown:
As slump increase, water content increases means

workability increases.

Compaction factor

$=\frac{\text { Weight of partially compacted concrete }}{\text { Weight of fully compacted concrete }}$

$\therefore$ Compaction factor will also increase.

The time required for complete remoulding in

seconds is considered as a measure of

workability and is expressed as the number of

Vee-Bee seconds.

$\therefore$ As workability increases, Vee-Bee time decreases.

pp:ce:2015:q8.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 8
pp:ce:2015:q8.question: The development length of a deformed reinforncement bar can be expressed as (1/k) $(\phi \sigma _{s}/\tau _{bd})$. From the IS: 456-2000, the value of k can be calculated as________.

primary.subtopicLabel: Shear, Torsion, Bond, Anchorage and Development Length

detailed_solution.concept: RCC Structures - Shear, Torsion, Bond, Anchorage and Development Length
detailed_solution.markdown:
Bond strength of concrete

$$\begin{aligned} &=\text{ Tensile force in steel}\\ \tau_{b d} \times\left(L_{d} \pi \phi\right)&=0.87 f_{y} \times\left(\frac{\pi}{4} \phi^{2}\right)\\ \Rightarrow \quad L_{d}&=\frac{0.87 f_{y} \phi}{4 \tau_{b d}} \\ \end{aligned}$$

For deformed bars $\tau_{\text {bd }}$ value is increased by 60 %

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad L_{d}&=\frac{\phi \sigma_{s}}{4 \times\left(1.6 \tau_{b d}\right)}=\frac{\phi \sigma_{s}}{6.4 \tau_{b d}}\\ \therefore \quad k&=6.4 \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q16.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 16
pp:ce:2015:q16.question: In a two-dimensional steady flow field, in a certain region of the x-y plane, the velocity component in the x-direction is given by $v_{x}=x^{2}$ and the density varies as $\rho =\frac{1}{x}$. Which of the following is a valid expression for the velocity component in the y- direction, $v_{y}$ ?

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Fluid Kinematics
detailed_solution.markdown:
Continuity equation in steady flow.

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{\partial(\rho u)}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial(\rho v)}{\partial y} &=0 \\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left[\frac{1}{x} \cdot x^{2}\right]+\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(\frac{1}{x} \cdot v_{y}\right) &=0 \\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x}(x)+\frac{1}{x} \frac{\partial v_{y}}{x \partial y} &=0 \\ 1+\frac{1}{x} \frac{\partial v_{y}}{\partial y} &=0 \\ -x &=\frac{\partial v_{y}}{\partial y} \end{aligned}$$

On integrating both sides

$v_{y}=-x y$

It may be treated as an open channel flow when it is flowing just full, i.e., the water level just touches the crest. The discharge in this condition is denoted by $Q_{full}$. Similarly, the discharge when the pipe is flowing half-full i.e., with a flow depth of 0.5m, is denoted by $Q_{half}$. The ratio $Q_{full}/Q_{half}$ is:

$$\begin{aligned} \text{slope,} \quad S&=\frac{1}{1000} \\ n&=0.01\\ \frac{Q_{full}}{Q_{half}} &= \frac{\left[\frac{A}{N}(R)^{2/3}S^{1/2} \right]_{\text{full}}}{\left[\frac{A}{N}(R)^{2/3}S^{1/2} \right]_{\text{half}}}\\ &=\frac{\left[AR^{2/3} \right ]_{\text{full}}}{\left[AR^{2/3} \right ]_{\text{half}}}\\ R_{\text{full}}&=R_{\text{Half}}=\frac{d}{4}\\ &=\frac{\frac{\pi d^{2}}{4}}{\frac{\pi d^{2}}{8}}=2 \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q26.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 26
pp:ce:2015:q26.question:
The smallest and largest Eigen values of the following matrix are :
$$\begin{bmatrix} 3 &-2 &2 \\ 4 &-4 &6 \\ 2 &-3 &5 \end{bmatrix}$$

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Linear Algebra
detailed_solution.markdown:
For eigen values

$$\begin{aligned} \left | A-\lambda I \right |&=0 \\ \begin{vmatrix} 3-\lambda & -2 &2 \\ 4 & -4-\lambda &6 \\ 2 & -3 & 5-\lambda \end{vmatrix}&=0 \\ \left ( 3-\lambda \right )\left ( -20+4\lambda -5\lambda +\lambda ^{2}+18 \right ) &\\ +2 \left ( 20-4\lambda -12 \right )+2\left ( -12+8+2\lambda \right )&=0 \\  \lambda ^{3}-4\lambda ^{2}+5\lambda -2&=0\end{aligned}$$

Only 1 and 2 satisfy this equation.

$\lambda =1,\: 1,\: 2$

Hence, Smallest eigen value =1 and

Largest eigen value =2

pp:ce:2015:q27.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 27
pp:ce:2015:q27.question: The quadratic equation $x^{2}-4x+4=0$ is to be solved numerically, starting with the initial guess $x_0=3$. The Newton-Raphson method is applied once to get a new estimate and then the Secant method is applied once using the initial guess and this new estimate. The estimated value of the root after the application of the Secant method is __________.

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Numerical Methods
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned}  f\left ( x \right )&=x^{2}-4x+4 \\   {f}'\left ( x \right )&=2x-4 \\   x_{0}&=3 \\   f\left ( 3 \right )&=1, {f}'\left ( 3 \right )=2 \\ \text{By Newton } & \text{Rapshon method,}\\   x_{1}&=x_{0}-\frac{f\left ( x_{0} \right )}{{f}'_{x_{0}}} \\    &=3-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{5}{2} \\   f\left ( \frac{5}{2} \right )&=\frac{25}{4}-10+4=\frac{1}{4} \\ & \text{By Secant method,}\\   x_{2}&=x_{1}-\frac{\left ( x_{1}-x_{0} \right )f\left ( x_{1} \right )}{f\left ( x_{1} \right )-f\left ( x_{0} \right )} \\    &=\frac{f_{1}x_{0}-f_{0}x_{1}}{f_{1}-f_{0}} \\    &=\frac{\left ( \frac{1}{4}\times 3 \right )-\left ( 1\times \frac{5}{2} \right )}{\frac{1}{4}-1} \\    &=\frac{7}{3}=2.33 \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q28.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 28
pp:ce:2015:q28.question:
Consider the following differential equation:
$x(ydx+xdy)\cos \frac{y}{x}=y(xdy-ydx)\sin \frac{y}{x}$
Which of the following is the solution of the above equation (c is an arbitrary constant)?

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Ordinary Differential Equation
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} x\left ( ydx+xdy \right )\cos \frac{y}{x}&=y\left ( xdy-ydx \right )\sin \frac{y}{x} \\ \frac{ydx+xdy}{xdy-ydx}&=\frac{y}{x}\tan \frac{y}{x}\\ \text{Let }  y&=v \cdot x \\   dy&=vdx+xdv \\ \frac{vxdx+vxdx+x^{2}dv}{vxdx+x^{2}dv-vxdx}&=v\tan v \\ \frac{xdv+2vdx}{xdv}&=v\tan v \\ 1+\frac{2v}{x}\frac{dx}{dv}&=v\tan v \\ \frac{2v}{x}\frac{dx}{dv}&=v\tan v-1 \\ 2\frac{dx}{x}&=\left ( \tan v-\frac{1}{v} \right )dv \end{aligned}$$

Integrating both sides.

$$\begin{aligned}2\log x&=\log \left | \sec v \right |-\log v+\log c \\ \Rightarrow \;\; x^{2}&=\frac{c\sec v}{v} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; x^{2}\frac{y}{x}&=c\sec \frac{y}{x} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; xy\cos \frac{y}{x}&=c \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q29.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 29
pp:ce:2015:q29.question:
Consider the following complex function:
$f(z)=\frac{9}{(z-1)(z+2)^{2}}$
Which of the following is one of the residues of the above function?

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
detailed_solution.markdown:
$f(z)$ has poles at $z=1, -2$

Residue of $f(z)$ at [/latex](z=1)[/latex]

$$\begin{aligned}  &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 1}\left ( z-1 \right )f\left ( z \right ) \\   &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 1}\frac{9}{\left ( z+2 \right )^{2}} \\&=1 \end{aligned}$$

Residue of $f(z)$ at $(z=-2)$

$$\begin{aligned}  &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 2}\frac{d}{dz^{2-1}}\left [ \left ( z+2 \right )^{2}f\left ( z \right ) \right ] \\   &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 2}\frac{d}{dz}\left ( \frac{9}{z-1} \right ) \\   &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 2}\left ( \frac{9}{\left ( z-1 \right )^{2}} \right ) \\   &=-1\end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q30.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 30
pp:ce:2015:q30.question: The directional derivative of the field $u(x,y,z)=x^{2}-3xy$ in the direction of the vector $(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})$ and point (2, -1, 4) is _________.

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned}u (x, y, z)&=x^{2}-3yz \\  \triangledown u&=2x\hat{i}-3z\hat{j}-3y\hat{k} \\  \triangledown ul_{at\: \left ( 2,\, -1\, 4 \right )}&=4\hat{i}+12\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\\ &\text{Directional derivative}\\   &= \left ( 4\hat{i}+12\hat{j}-3\hat{k} \right ).\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}}{\sqrt{6}} \\   &= \frac{4-12-6}{\sqrt{6}} =-\frac{14}{\sqrt{6}} \\   &= -\frac{7\sqrt{6}}{3}=-5.715\end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q33.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 33
pp:ce:2015:q33.question: Consider the singly reinforced beam section given below (left figure). The stress block parameters for the cross-section from IS: 456 : 2000 are also given below (right figure). The moment of resistance for the given section by the limit state method is ________ kN-m

primary.subtopicLabel: Working Stress and Limit State Method

detailed_solution.concept: RCC Structures - Working Stress and Limit State Method
detailed_solution.markdown:

pp:ce:2015:q34.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 34
pp:ce:2015:q34.question: For formation of collapse mechanism in the following figure, the minimum value of $P_{u}$ is $cM_{p}/L$. $M_{p}$ and $3M_{p}$ denote the plastic moment capacities of beam sections as shown in this figure. The value of c is _____.

detailed_solution.concept: Design of Steel Structures - Plastic Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} L\phi&=3L\theta \\ \phi&=3\theta \\4M_{P}\theta +2M_{P}\phi &=PL\phi \\ \frac{4M_{P}\phi }{3}+2M_{P}\phi &=PL\phi \\ \frac{10M_{P}\phi }{3}&=PL\phi \\ P=\frac{10M_{P}}{3L} \; \Rightarrow \; C&=\frac{10}{3}=3.33 \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q35.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 35
pp:ce:2015:q35.question: A tapered circular rod of diameter varying from 20 mm to 10 mm is connected to another uniform circular rod of diameter 10 mm as shown in the following figure. Both bars are made of same material with the modulus of elasticity, $E=2\times 10^{5}$ MPa. When subjected to a load $P=30\pi kN$ , the deflection at point A is ______ mm.

primary.subtopicLabel: Properties of Metals, Stress and Strain

detailed_solution.concept: Solid Mechanics - Properties of Metals, Stress and Strain
detailed_solution.markdown: Total elongation, $$\begin{aligned} \Delta &=\Delta_{A B}+\Delta_{B C} \\ &=\frac{P L}{A E}+\frac{4 P L}{\pi d_{1} d_{2} E} \\ &=\frac{30 \pi \times 1.5}{\frac{\pi \times(0.01)^{2}}{4} \times 2 \times 10^{5}} \\ &+\frac{30 \pi \times 2}{\frac{\pi \times(0.01) \times(0.02)}{4} \times 2 \times 10^{5}} \\ &=9+6=15 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q36.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 36
pp:ce:2015:q36.question: Two beams are connected by a linear spring as shown in the following figure. For a load P as shown in the figure, the percentage of the applied load P carried by the spring is __________.

detailed_solution.concept: Solid Mechanics - Deflection of Beams
detailed_solution.markdown: $\Delta_{\text {spring }}=\Delta_{B}-\Delta_{D}$ Compression of spring $$\begin{aligned} =\frac{(P-R) L^{3}}{3 E I}-\frac{R L^{3}}{3 E I}&=\frac{R}{K_{S}} \\ \frac{(P-R) L^{3}}{3 E I}-\frac{R L^{3}}{3 E I}&=\frac{R \times\left(2 L^{3}\right)}{3 E I}\\ (P-A)-R &=2 R \\ P &=4 R \\ R &=\frac{P}{4} \end{aligned}$$ % force carried by spring =25 %

pp:ce:2015:q37.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 37
pp:ce:2015:q37.question: For the 2D truss with the applied loads shown below, the strain energy in the member XY is _______ kN-m. For member XY, assume AE = 30 kN, where A is cross-section area and E is the modulus of elasticity.

pp:ce:2015:q38.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 38
pp:ce:2015:q38.question: An earth embankment is to be constructed with compacted cohesionless soil. The volume of the embankment is 5000 $m^{3}$ and the target dry unit weight is 16.2 $kN/m^{3}$. Three nearby sites (see figure blwo) have been identified from where the required soil can be transported to the construction site. The void ratios (e) of different sites are shown in the figure. Assume the specific gravity of soil to be 2.7 for all three sites. If the cost of transportation per km is twice the cost of excavation per $m^{3}$ of borrow pits, which site would you choose as the most economic solution? (Use unit weight of water = 10$kN/m^{3}$)

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Properties of Soils
detailed_solution.markdown:
Volume of solids at embankment,

$$\begin{aligned}

V_{s} &=\frac{W_{s}}{G_{s} \gamma_{w}} \\

V_{s} &=\frac{16.2 \times 5000}{27 \times 10} \mathrm{m}^{3} \\

&=3000 \mathrm{m}^{3}

\end{aligned}$$

Volume of solids will remain constant.

also,

$$\begin{aligned}

V &=V_{V}+V_{s} \\

&=e V_{s}+V_{s}=V_{s}(1+e) \\

V &=3000(1+e) \\

V_{X} &=3000 \times 1.6=4800 \mathrm{m}^{3} \\

V_{Y} &=3000 \times 1.7=5100 \mathrm{m}^{3} \\

v_{z} &=3000 \times 1.64=4920 \mathrm{m}^{3}

\end{aligned}$$

Let cost of excavation be $\alpha / \mathrm{m}^{3}$

$$\begin{aligned}

P_{X} &=4800 \alpha+140 \times \alpha \times 2 \\

&=5080 \alpha \\

P_{Y} &=5100 \alpha+80 \times \alpha \times 2 \\

&=5260 \alpha \\

P_{Z} &=4920 \alpha+100 \times \alpha \times 2 \\

&=5120 \alpha

\end{aligned}$$

Hence $P_{X}$ is least.

Hence total cost for site X is least.

pp:ce:2015:q39.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 39
pp:ce:2015:q39.question: A water tank is to be constructed on the soil deposit shown in the figure below. A circular footing of diameter 3 m and depth of embedment 1 m has been designed to support the tank. The total vertical load to be taken by the footing is 1500 kN. Assume the unit weight of water as 10 $kN/m^{3}$ and the load dispersion pattern as 2V:1H. The expected settlement of the tank due to primary consolidation of the clay layer is ________ mm.

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Consolidation of Soils
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \Delta H &=\frac{C_{C} H_{0}}{1+e_{0}} \log _{10}\left[\frac{\bar{\sigma}_{0}+\Delta \bar{\sigma}}{\bar{\sigma}_{0}}\right] \\ H_{0} &=\text { Thickness of clay layer } \\ &=10 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$ $\bar{\sigma}_{0}=$ Effective stress before application of load at the centre of clay layer $$\begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma}_{0}&=(15 \times 2)+(18-10) \times 6+(18-10) \times 5 \\ &= 118 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$ $\Delta \bar{\sigma}=$ Increase in effective stress due to the structural weight at the centre of clay layer $$\begin{aligned} \Delta \bar{\sigma} &=\frac{1500}{\frac{\pi}{4} \times(3+12)^{2}}=8.488 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \Delta H &=\frac{0.3 \times 10}{1+0.7} \log _{10}\left(\frac{118+8.488}{118}\right) \\ &=0.053236 \mathrm{m}=53.236 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q40.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 40
pp:ce:2015:q40.question:
A 20 m thick clay layer is sandwiched between a silty sand layer and a gravelly sand layer. The layer experiences 30 mm settlement in 2 years.

Given:
$$T_{v}=\left\{\begin{matrix} \frac{\pi }{4}\left ( \frac{U}{100} \right )^{2}& forU\leq 60\%\\ 1.781-0.933\log_{10}(100-U)& for U>60\%\end{matrix}\right.$$

Where $T_v$ is the time factor and U is the degree consolidation in $\%$.
If the coefficient of consolidation of the layer is 0.003 $cm^{2}/s$, the deposit will experience a total of 50 mm settlement in the next _______ years.

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Consolidation of Soils
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} T_{v}&=\frac{C_{v} t}{d^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad T_{v}&=\frac{0.003 \times 2 \times 86400 \times 365}{\left(\frac{20}{2} \times 100\right)^{2}}\\ T_{v}&=0.1892 \lt 0.02827 \\ T_{v}&=\frac{\pi}{4} U^{2}=0.1892 &(\therefore U \lt 60 \%)\\ \Rightarrow \quad U&=0.4908 \\ \Rightarrow \quad&\text{Total consolidation}\\ &=\frac{30}{0.4908}=61.12 \mathrm{mm}\\ \end{aligned}$$ Degree of consolidation for 50 mm settlement $$\begin{aligned} U &=\frac{50}{61.12}=0.818=81.8 \% \\ \Rightarrow \quad T_{v} &=0.60835=\frac{C_{v} t}{H^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad t &=\frac{0.60835 \times(10)^{2}}{0.003 \times 10^{-4}} \\ &=6.43 \text { years } \end{aligned}$$ $\Rightarrow$Additional number of years =4.43

pp:ce:2015:q42.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 42
pp:ce:2015:q42.question:
A square footing (2m x 2m) is subjected to an inclined point load P as shown in the figure below. The water table is located well below the base of the footing. Considering one-way eccentricity, the net safe load carrying capacity of the footing for a factor of safety of 3.0 is _________ kN.

The following factor may be used:

Bearing capacity factors: $N_{q}$ =33.3, $N_{\gamma }$=37.16; Shape factor:$F_{qs }=F_{\gamma s }$=1.314; Depth factors : $F_{q d }=F_{\gamma d }$=1.133; Inclination factors: $F_{q i }$=0.444, $F_{\gamma i }$=0.02

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Shallow Foundation and Bearing Capacity
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} B'&= B-2e_x\\ &= 2-2 \times 0.15\\ &= 1.7m \end{aligned}$$ As per Meyerhof theory $$\begin{aligned} q_u&=CN_cS_cd_ci_c+\gamma D_fN_qd_qi_q\\ &+0.5B'\gamma N_\gamma S_\gamma d_ri_r\\ q_u&=18 \times 1(1.314 \times 1.113 \times 0.444) \times 33.3\\ &+10.5 \times 1.7 \times 18 \times 37.16 \\ & \times (1.314 \times 1.113 \times 0.02)\\ &=405.84 \; kN/m^2\\ q_{ns}&=\frac{q_u-\sigma }{F}=\frac{q_u-\gamma D_f}{F}\\ &=\frac{405.84-18 \times 1}{3}\\ &=129.28 \; kN/m^2\\ &\text{Net safe load}\\ &=q_{ns} \times \text{Area}\\ &=q_{ns} \times (B' \times L)\\ &=129.28 \times 1.7 \times 2\\ &=439.55\; kN \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q43.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 43
pp:ce:2015:q43.question: Two reservoirs are connected through a 930 m long, 0.3 m diameter pipe, which has a gate valve. The pipe entrance is sharp (loss coefficient = 0.5) and the valve is half-open (loss coefficient = 5.5). The head difference between the two reservoirs is 20 m. Assume the friction factor for the pipe as 0.03 and g = 10 $m/s^{2}$. The discharge in the pipe accounting for all minor and major losses is _________ $m^{3}/s$ .

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Flow Through Pipes
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} L&=930 \mathrm{m} \\ D&= 0.3 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$ Apply energy equation between A and B $$\begin{aligned} 20&=\frac{0.5 V^{2}}{2 g}+\frac{(0.03)(930) V^{2}}{2 g(0.3)}+\frac{5.5 V^{2}}{2 g}+\frac{V^{2}}{20} \\\ 20&=\frac{(0.03)(930)}{(03)} \frac{v^{2}}{20}+\frac{70 v^{2}}{20} \\ 20&=\frac{100 v^{2}}{2 g} \\ V&=2 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{se} \\ a&=\frac{\pi}{4}(0.3)^{2}(2) \\ Q&=0.1414 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{sec} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q44.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 44
pp:ce:2015:q44.question: A hydraulic jump is formed in a 2 m wide rectangular channel which is horizontal and frictionless. The post-jump depth and velocity are 0.8 m and 1 $m/s$, respectively. The pre-jump velocity is _______$m/s$ (use g=10 $m/s^{2}$).

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} y_{2} &=0.8 \mathrm{m} \\ v_{2} &=1 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ F_{f_{2}} &=\frac{v_{2}}{\sqrt{g D}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10 \times \frac{0.8 \times 2}{2}}} \\ F_{f_{2}} &=0.3535 \\ y_{1} &=\frac{y_{2}}{2}\left(-1+\sqrt{1+8 F_{12}^{2}}\right) \\ &=\frac{0.8}{2}\left(-1+\sqrt{1+8 \times 0.3535^{2}}\right) \\ &=0.165643 \\ \Rightarrow \quad v_{1} y_{1} &=v_{2} y_{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad v_{1} &=\frac{1 \times 0.8}{0.165643}=4.83 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q45.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 45
pp:ce:2015:q45.question: A short reach of a 2 m wide rectangular open channel has its bed level rising in the direction of flow at a slope of 1 in 10000. It carries a discharge of 4 $m^{3}/s$ and its Manning's roughness coefficient is 0.01. The flow in this reach is gradually varying. At a certain section in this reach, the depth of flow was measured as 0.5 m. The rate of change of the water depth with distance, dy/dx, at this section is ____ (use g = 10 $m/s^{2}$).

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Adverb slope }&= -\frac{1}{1000}\\\\ Q &=4 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s} \\ n &=0.01 \\ y &=0.5 \mathrm{m} \\ \frac{d y}{d x} &=\frac{S_{0}-S_{f}}{1-F_{t}^{2}} \\ F_{r} &=\frac{V}{\sqrt{g y}}=\frac{Q}{2 y \sqrt{g y}} \\ &=\frac{4}{2 \times 0.5 \sqrt{10 \times 0.5}}=1.789 \\ R &=\frac{A}{P}=\frac{2 \times 0.5}{2+2 \times 0.5}=\frac{1}{3} \\ Q &=\frac{1}{n} A R^{2 / 3} S_{f}^{1 / 2} \end{aligned}$$

On solving for $S_{f}$

$$\begin{aligned} S_{f}^{1 / 2} &=6.923 \times 10^{-3} \\ \frac{d y}{d x} &=\frac{-\frac{1}{10000}-6.923 \times 10^{-3}}{1-(1.789)^{2}} \\ &=3.191 \times 10^{-3} \simeq 0.0032 \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q46.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 46
pp:ce:2015:q46.question: The drag force $F_{D}$, on a sphere kept in a uniform flow field depends on the diameter of the sphere, D; flow velocity, V; fluid density, $\rho$; and dynamic viscosity, $\mu$. Which of the following options represents the non-dimensional parameters which could be used to analyze this problem?

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Dimensional Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{For sphere,}\quad A&=\frac{\pi}{4} D^{2} \\ F_{D} &=C_{D} \times \frac{1}{2} \times p \times A \times V^{2} \\ F_{D} &=C_{D} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \rho \times\left(\frac{\pi}{4} D^{2}\right) \times V^{2} \\ \frac{F_{D}}{\rho D^{2} V^{2}} &=\frac{1}{2} \times\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \times C_{D} \end{aligned}$$

Hence, right hand side is dimensionless, so $\frac{F_{0}}{\rho D^{2} V^{2}}$ should also be a dimensionless parameter.

Option (C) $\frac{F_{0}}{\rho V^{2} D^{2}}, \frac{\rho V D}{\mu}$

pp:ce:2015:q47.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 47
pp:ce:2015:q47.question: In a catchment, there are four rain-gauge stations, P, Q, R, and S. Normal annual precipitation values at these stations are 780 mm, 850 mm, 920 mm, and 980 mm respectively. In the year 2013, stations Q, R, and S, were operative but P was not. Using the normal ratio method, the precipitation at station P for the year 2013 has been established as 860 mm. If the observed precipitation at station Q and R for the year 2013 were 930 mm and 1010 mm, respectively; what was the observed precipitation (in mm) at station S for that year?

primary.subtopicLabel: Precipitation and General Aspects of Hydrology

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Hydrology - Precipitation and General Aspects of Hydrology
detailed_solution.markdown:
Let $P_{p}=$ Precipitation in 2013 at station P

$N_{p}=$ Noramal annual precipitation at station P

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{P_{p}}{N_{p}}&=\frac{1}{3}\left [ \frac{P_{Q}}{N_{q}}+\frac{P_{R}}{N_{R}}+\frac{P_{S}}{N_{S}} \right ]\\ \frac{860}{780}&=\frac{1}{3}\left [ \frac{930}{850}+\frac{1010}{920}+\frac{P_{S}}{980} \right ] \\ \Rightarrow \;\; P_{s}&=1093.43 mm \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q49.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 49
pp:ce:2015:q49.question:
The concentration of Sulfur Dioxide ($SO_{2}$) in ambient atmosphere was measured as 30 $\mu g/m^{3}$. Under the same conditions, the above $SO_{2}$ concentration expressed in ppm is ___________.

Given: (P/(RT) = 41.6 $mol/m^{3}$; where, P=Pressure; T=Temperature; R=universal gas constant; Molecular weight of $SO_{2}$= 64.

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Air and Noise Pollution
detailed_solution.markdown:
1 $m^{3}$ of air has 30$\mu g\; \; SO_{2}$

$10^{6}$$m^{3}$ of air has 30g $SO_{2}$

$$\begin{aligned} 30g\; SO_{2} &=\frac{30}{64}\text{mole}\; SO_{2} \\ \text{From}\; PV &=nRT \\ V &=\frac{nRT}{P}=\frac{n}{P/RT} \\ &=\frac{\left ( 30/64 \right )}{41.6\; mol/m^{3}} \\ \text{Volume of}SO_{2} &=\frac{30}{64\times 41.6} \\ &=0.01127\; m^{3} \end{aligned}$$

$\Rightarrow$ Concentration of $SO_{2}$ in PPM=0.0113 ppm

pp:ce:2015:q50.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 50
pp:ce:2015:q50.question:
Consider a primary sedimentation tank (PST) in a water treatment plant with Surface Overflow Rate (SOR) of 40 $m^{3}/m^2/d$. The diameter of the spherical particle which will have 90 percent theoretical removal efficiency in this tank is_________ $\mu m$. Assume that settling velocity of the particle in water described by Stokes' Law.

Given: Density of water = 1000 $kg/m^{3}$; Density of particle = 2650 $kg/m^{3}$; g = 9.81$m/s^{2}$; Kinematic viscosity of water $(v) = 1.10 \times 10^{-6} m^{2}/s$

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Water Treatment
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} \text { \% removal } &=\frac{V_{s}^{\prime}}{V_{s}} \times 100 \\ V_{s}^{\prime} &=0.9 \times V_{s} \\ &=0.9 \times \text { Overfiow rate } \\ V_{s}^{\prime} &=\frac{0.9 \times 40}{86400} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \frac{(G-1) g d^{2}}{18 \mathrm{v}} &=\frac{0.9 \times 40}{86400} \\ d &=\sqrt{\frac{0.9 \times 40 \times 18 \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{w}} \mathrm{V}}{86400 \times\left(G_{s}-1\right) \times \rho_{\mathrm{w}} \times g}} \\ &=\sqrt{\frac{0.9 \times 40 \times 18 \times 1.1 \times 10^{-6}}{86400 \times 1.64 \times 9.81}} \\ &=2.2576 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{m}=22.576 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q51.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 51
pp:ce:2015:q51.question:
The acceleration time relationship for a vehicle subjected to non-uniform acceleration is,
$\frac{\mathrm{d}v }{\mathrm{d} t}=(\alpha -\beta v_{0})e^{-\beta t}$
Where, v is the speed in m/s, t is the time in s, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are parameters, and $v_{0}$ is the initial speed in m/s. If the accelerating behavior of a vehicle, whose drive intends to overtake a slow moving vehicle ahead, is described as,
$\frac{\mathrm{d} v}{\mathrm{d} t}=(\alpha -\beta v)$
considering $\alpha =2 m/s^{2}$, $\beta =0.05s^{-1}$ and $\frac{\mathrm{d}v }{\mathrm{d} t}=1.3 m/s^{2}$ at t=3s, the distance(in m) travelled by the vehicle in 35s is _______.

primary.subtopicLabel: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} &\frac{d v}{d t}=\alpha-\beta v\\ &\Rightarrow \quad \int \frac{d v}{(\alpha-\beta v)}=\int d t\\ &\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\ln (\alpha-\beta v)}{-\beta}=t+C\\ &\text { at } t=3 \text { sec, } \frac{d v}{d t}=\alpha-\beta v=1.3 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\\ &\Rightarrow \frac{\ln (1.3)}{-0.05}=3+c \Rightarrow c=-8.247\\ &\therefore \quad \ln (2-0.05 \times v)=(t-8.247)(-0.05)\\ &\Rightarrow 2-0.05 \times v=1.51 \mathrm{e}^{-0.05 t}\\ &\Rightarrow v=\frac{d s}{d t}=40-30.21 e^{-0.05 t}\\ &\Rightarrow s=40 t+604.15 e^{-0.05 t}+c^{\prime}\\ &\therefore \quad \text { at } t=0, s=0 \Rightarrow c^{\prime}=-604.15\\ &\Rightarrow \quad s=40 t+604.15 e^{-0.05 t}-604.15\\ &\text { at } t=35 \mathrm{sec}\\ &\Rightarrow \quad s=40 \times 35+604.15 \mathrm{e}^{-0.05 \times 35}-604\\ &\Rightarrow \quad s=900.84 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2015:q52.title: GATE CE 2015 | Set 1 | Question: 52
pp:ce:2015:q52.question: On a circular curve, the rate of superelevation is e. While negotiating the curve a vehicle comes to a stop. It is seen that the stopped vehicle does not slide inwards (in the radial direction). The coefficient of side friction is f. Which of the following is true :

$\because$ Obserbed FB of AO

= Observed BB of OA

$=120^{\circ}40^{\circ}$

$127^{\circ}20^{\circ}$

Error $= MB = TB =127^{\circ}20^{\circ}=120^{\circ}40^{\circ}$

$==2^{\circ}20^{\circ}$

Correction $=+2^{\circ}20^{\circ}$

Local attraction at station A

$=+2^{\circ}20^{\circ}=2^{\circ}20^{\circ}E$

$\therefore$ Magnetic FB of $AB=N76^{\circ}50^{\circ}E$

$\delta = 2^{\circ}E$ and local attraction $=2^{\circ}20^{\circ}E$

$\therefore$ TB of FB of AB $= 70^{\circ}50^{\circ}+2^{\circ}20^{\circ}+2^{\circ}$

$=N84^{\circ}10^{\prime}E$
